reality_delta: The plan would add a contract, an append-only ledger, and a runnable boundary-check CLI, but the described checks rely on directory placement, self-declared privacy markers, and ledger coverage rather than verifying that content is actually desensitized. A private body could satisfy all listed checks while still containing identity material or credentials, so the intended reality—private content is kept out of the public repo—may not actually change.
main_concern: The boundary-check validates metadata (directory, marker, ledger entry) instead of substance (desensitized content), producing passable evidence that can mask real leakage.
top_risks: Marker/directory policy is bypassable by mislabeling a private body as public and appending a ledger line, allowing identity material into the public repo while checks pass.
promotion-ledger is only append-only in name unless protected by signature, authority, or tamper-evident link; fake promotion records can satisfy coverage checks without real review.
No mandatory enforcement gate is described, so the check remains opt-in and can be skipped during actual promotion.
missing_evidence: Current schema for privacy markers, public/private directory boundaries, and how source_refs are resolved without reading Cap private content.
Ledger authority/integrity design: who appends, how entries are signed or bound to a desensitization review, and rollback handling.
End-to-end demonstration that a realistic private/credential payload is rejected before reaching the public index or ledger.
minimum_fix: Add content-level desensitization classification (not just markers), bind ledger entries to an authoritative signer or review artifact, and attach boundary-check to a mandatory promotion/CI gate that blocks merge on failure; maintain adversarial negative samples including real-looking private identity and credential patterns.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The deliverables are all self-generated artifacts; passing boundary-check does not prove a real private payload was ever stopped. Require a demonstrated rejection of a synthetic private body before promotion.

user_intent_alignment: Partial. The plan honors append-only, deduplication, and index-first structure, but it weakens the core intent that public content be desensitized and free of private identity material by relying on self-reported metadata rather than verifying and enforcing content safety.
